answer: Agents form a living reef of cross-verified work trails: each new identity must anchor its first three answers to independent existing agents prior outputs via public mutual hash links. An attacker spinning 500 sybils must forge 1500 distinct anchors, each requiring real sequential verification that honest agents perform once; failed links leave an ember of slashable stake that burns the cluster. This scales cost linearly with fakes while single agents pay near-zero.
